items.title: Norman Mason Interview, 1960-02-06
items.q: I remember when I was interested in, in, in, in concert, in concert music. You have, America had at that time, uh, your greatest, uh, your greatest trumpet player was Herbert Clark.

ctx.x: Well, like you said, the people are, I guess they, they're asking for more simple things. That's why, uh, you see. Well, uh, you see. A lot of them. That's one reason you have to play the same so much.

Yeah. Well, you know, uh, I, I remember when I was a boy, I remember, well, I remember when I was interested in, in, in, in concert, in concert music. You have, America had at that time, uh, your greatest, uh, your greatest trumpet player was Herbert Clark. Mm-hmm. Uh, your greatest trombone player was Arthur Pryor. You see, they were the two guys. I noticed, uh, uh, Herbert Clark, uh, what attracted, uh, me to his, his playing. He always plays a simple tune. He plays, uh, a warring, plotting tune. And, uh,…
